The statement conveys a deep negative shock to activity and employment but pairs it with a strong policy backstop. Keeping the funds rate at the effective lower bound and pledging ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases and repo operations is consistent with Taylor-rule-type prescriptions under large slack and below-target inflation (Taylor 1993; Woodford 2003) and with New Keynesian guidance that forward-looking policy and balance-sheet tools help anchor inflation expectations and transmit accommodation when conventional space is limited (Svensson 1997; Galí and Gertler 1999; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005). The focus on “smooth market functioning” and credit flow reflects credit-channel and agency-cost evidence that easing financial constraints supports real activity (Oliner and Rudebusch 1996; Ang and Piazzesi 2003 on term-structure transmission). Acknowledging improved financial conditions alongside persistent downside risks tilts the overall tone from strongly negative to moderately negative.
